input: Dye and re-grout the bathroom vanity countertop

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The countertop material (tile, cultured marble, solid surface, etc.) determines whether dyeing is even viable and which products to use — some surfaces cannot be dyed at all.
Knowing whether this is a solo DIY project or involves a hired professional changes the complexity of steps, tool recommendations, and budget guidance.
The current condition of the grout (cracked, stained, mouldy, or just discoloured) determines how much removal work is needed before re-grouting.
The target colour for both the dye and the new grout affects product selection and how much prep (e.g., stripping sealant, priming) is required.
A tight budget may rule out professional-grade dyes or professional labour; a tight timeline affects whether multi-day cure times are acceptable.
Access to tools (grout saw, sponges, sealer applicators) and how soon the bathroom needs to be back in use affects the sequencing and pacing of the job.
Understanding whether the goal is a like-new appearance, a colour change, or simply sealing problem areas determines the standard the finished result must meet.

gold.taskTitle: Dye and re-grout bathroom vanity countertop
gold.taskDescription: Refresh the bathroom vanity countertop by dyeing the surface and replacing or renewing the grout lines.

questions.title: What material is your countertop made of?
questions.description: Identify the countertop surface type — e.g., ceramic tile, cultured marble, natural stone, solid surface — since this dictates which dyes and grout products are compatible.

questions.title: Are you doing this yourself or hiring someone?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a DIY project or a professional job, as this shapes tool lists, skill-level guidance, and overall plan complexity.

questions.title: What is the current condition of the grout?
questions.description: Determine whether the grout is cracked, deeply stained, mouldy, or just discoloured, so the correct level of removal and prep work can be planned.

questions.title: What colour are you aiming for on the dye and grout?
questions.description: Understand the target finish colours for both the countertop surface dye and the new grout to guide product selection and any necessary priming steps.

questions.title: What is your budget for this project?
questions.description: Establish a spending limit to filter product recommendations between consumer-grade and professional-grade dyes, sealers, and tools.

questions.title: How soon does the bathroom need to be usable again?
questions.description: Determine the available downtime window, since dyes and grout sealers often require 24–72 hours of cure time before the surface can get wet.

questions.title: What does a successful result look like to you?
questions.description: Define the finish standard — a full colour transformation, a like-new restoration, or simply sealing problem spots — to set the right scope and quality target.
